title: Exact-Cost Unary State Copy
statement: Let $x$ be a Boolean input word, let $B$ be a four-tape configuration, and let $q,q'$ be interpreter control states and $d$ a movement in $\{-1,0,1\}$. Suppose that in state $q$, whenever the table cell read is $1$, the interpreter moves the table and state heads right, writes $1$ at the state head, and remains in $q$; whenever the table cell read is $0$, it moves the table head by $d$, leaves the state tape unchanged, and enters $q'$. For natural numbers $n,j$ and Boolean lists $l,r$, if the table is $l$ followed by $n$ ones, then $0$, then $r$, running for exactly $n+1$ steps from state $q$ with table cursor $|l|$ and the unary state-$j$ tape at cursor $j+1$ yields state $q'$, table cursor $|l|+n+d$, and the unary state-$(j+n)$ tape at cursor $j+n+1$.
hypotheses_covered: $B$ is a four-tape configuration on input $x$
the transition from $q$ on table read $1$ writes $1$, moves both heads right, and stays in $q$
the transition from $q$ on table read $0$ leaves the state tape unchanged, moves the table head by $d$, and enters $q'$
the table has the specified concatenation form
replaced:
Let $q$ be an interpreter control state that, on every combination of reads
with table read $1$, stays in $q$, writes a $1$ at the state cursor, and
moves both the table and state cursors right; and on every combination with
table read $0$ passes to a state $q'$ with a fixed table movement
$d \in \{-1, 0, +1\}$ and no other change.  Suppose the table is
$l \cdot 1^n \cdot 0 \cdot r$, the state tape is the intact unary encoding of
an index $j$, the table cursor is $|l|$, and the state cursor is $j + 1$.
Then exactly $n + 1$ interpreter steps reach $q'$ with table cursor
$|l| + n + d$, state tape the intact unary encoding of $j + n$, and state
cursor $j + n + 1$; all other data are unchanged.  This single gadget serves
both initial-state extraction and live successor-state replacement.
